Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  October 2, 2025

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on October 2, 2025. Commissioner
Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:02 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Cynthia McLemore - District
  3, Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner at Large
  Absent:  Commissioner Octavio Padilla - District 2, Commissioner
  Christopher Beck - District 4

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  PRCS Director
  Teresa Estrada  PRCS Assistant Director
  Kesha Brady  Human Services Program Manager
  Brian McClure  Parks Administration Superintendent
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner McLemore and second by Commissioner Brown
that the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on October 2,
2025, be approved. The following roll call vote carried the motion:

Ayes: Commissioner Denmon, Commissioner McLemore, Commissioner Brown,
Noes: None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Parks Administration Superintendent Brian McClure
reported the following: Parks Division - Public Works started their lighting upgrade project
at Darby Park on October 1. It is my understanding that this will improve the park and
sports lighting. The project is scheduled to be completed in April. Park staff will be placing
mulch around the barbeque area at Edward Vincent Park as well as in the north side of City
Hall. Last year, California banned the sale of new gas powered landscape equipment like
leaf blowers, mowers and chainsaws. We just purchased 11 new electric leaf blowers as
well as six new hedge trimmers along with the batteries and chargers to support them.

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

Graffiti Division - In September, we experienced a spike in graffiti in Districts 1 and 2
especially at the intersection of Crenshaw and Manchester and at Edward Vincent Park.
Tree Division - The annual tree contract wrapped up last week by West Coast Arborist.
They accomplished everything that was scheduled for the 2024/25 fiscal year. We
purchased a new stump grinder for the Tree Division. We are lining up stumps to test it
out at Vincent Park. The Graffiti hotline is (310) 412-8739.

REPORT - RECREATION. Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department Assistant
Director Teresa Estrada reported the following: Harvest Festival – This year, we will be
hosting a Harvest Festival to celebrate the Fall season. While we typically celebrate with a
Halloween Festival, we did take into consideration that not all families celebrate
Halloween. The Harvest Festival will feature pumpkin decorating, games, face painting, a
magic show, and additional activities. Please join us on Saturday, October 18th, at
Inglewood City Hall’s south lawn from 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. Halloween Haunted House
– for those who do celebrate Halloween, we are having our annual Haunted House at
Darby Park on October 30th and 31st from 5:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. While we usually host our
haunted house at Rogers Park, due to the special election this year Rogers will be occupied.

REPORT - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Program Manager Kesha Brady reported on
the following: Senior Center Activities - Our Senior Center continues to grow, with notable
increases in participations numbers and programs. On October 6, we will be taking seniors
to The Long Beach Aquarium from 11:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. A program has been planned to
honor Breast Cancer Awareness Month on October 15, beginning at 10:00 a.m. - 11:00
a.m. with special poetry readings. Mercedes Aguirre of the LA County Department of
Mental Health will be conducting a presentation on “Mental Health and Stigma” on
October 20. Rie Fischman of The Center for Health Care Rights will be conducting a
presentation on “Getting Ready for Medicare’s Open Enrollment” on October 22. On
October 22, we will be taking seniors to El Camino College for a special “Spa Day” which
includes hair, nails, and facials. On October 23, we will screen the movie “Ladder 49" and
a Halloween Dance from 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. on October 31. Elderly Nutrition Program
the Senior Center serves approximately 460 seniors per week through home-delivered
meals for homebound seniors and congregate meals. We continue to offer fresh produce
on a weekly basis in partnership with the Social Justice Learning Institute, as well as
monthly shelf-stable meal boxes in collaboration with the Los Angeles Food Bank. Farmers'
Market cards have been distributed, and seniors have been able to take several trips to
the market from the center through our transportation services. We also work in
partnership with Los Angeles County to refer seniors to our center to receive Home
Delivered Meals and workshops focused on healthy eating habits. Through this same meal
program, we can provide our seniors with nourishing meals while they are on field trips
organized by the senior center, thanks to the support of our transportation and operations
managers. As our numbers continue to climb weekly in program participation, we look

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

forward to serving all of our seniors. Senior Transportation Services - the City of
Inglewood’s paratransit program continues to provide trips to seniors and the disabled
community in Inglewood and Hawthorne. We are expecting an addition to the bus
operator team bringing on a new full time bus operator at the start of October
2025. Transportation is also in the process of hiring a part time driver as well and look
forward to their arrival as well. We expect these new additions will enhance service levels
and reduce wait times. The department is also in the planning stages to conduct a
transportation workshop event to knowledge share all the transportation resources that
are available to our seniors and our disabled community. We look forward to it being an
eventful and educational event and as always, we continue to strive in providing
outstanding paratransit service to our seniors and our disabled community.

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department Director
Thomas Uwal reported on the following: Volunteer Appreciation Event - the Department
will host a Volunteer Appreciation Event at Edward Vincent Jr. Park (Veterans Building) on
Monday, September 29, 2025, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. This event is dedicated to
recognizing the contributions of our volunteers, whose commitment greatly enhances our
programming, community engagement, and overall service quality. We deeply value their
support and dedication. Commissioners are encouraged to join us in celebrating their
efforts. Park Safety Coordination Meeting with Inglewood Police Department - The
department continues to coordinate Park Safety Meetings with the Inglewood Police
Department. The next meeting is scheduled for Wednesday, October 22, 2025 at 11:00
a.m. This partnership addresses day-to-day park safety concerns, deters crime, and fosters
stronger relationships between staff and law enforcement. Regular collaboration ensures
staff feel supported when handling difficult situations while also promoting consistent
police presence in our parks. These meetings provide a valuable platform for exchanging
input and strategies to enhance public safety. Park Maintenance Staff Relocation - Parks
maintenance staff will be relocating from Edward Vincent Jr. Park to a temporary modular
office at the City Service Center on October 1, 2025. The existing Edward Vincent Jr. Park
facilities are outdated and scheduled for replacement. The Public Works Department is
currently in the design phase, with demolition and construction expected to begin in the
upcoming fiscal year. Department Newsletter - the Parks, Recreation and Community
Services Newsletter will be released during the second week of October 2025. The
newsletter will provide residents with updates on upcoming programs, classes, community
events, and departmental initiatives. It will also serve as a resource for residents to stay
connected with park activities, explore opportunities for all ages, and learn about ongoing
projects and improvements within the city’s parks system.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner McLemore brought attention to the streets
having tons of trash around the first of every month. Assistant Director Teresa Estrada
made mention of illegal dumping and suggested contacting Public Works to report it.
Commissioner Denmon stated coyotes have become a big problem at Darby Park and
suggests collaborating with someone to see how we can relocate them for safety reasons.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:37 p.m.
